We have the function 

$$
y={(\frac{1}{2x})}^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(\frac{1}{2x})}^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x})) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x}))+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x}))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x})+x\cdot ((2x)\cdot (-\frac{2}{(2x)^{2}})) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2x})-1 \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1 \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={(\frac{1}{2x})}^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-{(\frac{1}{2x})}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1) \\  & =-{(2x)}^{-x}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$
